ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the Arabic word كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (kayfa haaluka?) mean? (1 mark)
   A. and upon you peace (the reply)
   B. I
   C. welcome
   D. How are you? (to a boy)

2. Which greeting fits when you meet someone in the evening? (1 mark)
   A. sabaahu l-khayr
   B. ʿafwan
   C. masaa'u l-khayr
   D. maʿa s-salaama

3. How is the Arabic word أَنَا read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. maʿa s-salaama
   B. anaa
   C. sabaahu l-khayr
   D. as-salaamu ʿalaykum

4. Which Arabic sentence means "This is my father." (1 mark)
   A. هَذَا أَبِي
   B. أَبِي يَعْمَلُ
   C. هَذِهِ أُمِّي
   D. عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ

5. What does the Arabic sentence أَخِي يَلْعَبُ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My brother plays.
   B. I have a brother and a sister.
   C. This is my mother.
   D. This is my father.

6. What does the Arabic sentence مَنْ هَذَا؟ mean? (1 mark)
   A. This is my mother.
   B. I have a brother and a sister.
   C. This is my father.
   D. Who is this? (a boy or man)

7. How is the Arabic word مَطْبَخٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ghurfa
   B. sikkiin
   C. milʿaqa
   D. matbakh

8. What does the Arabic sentence أَلْعَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I play on Saturday.
   B. I go to school on Monday.
   C. There are seven days in a week.
   D. Today is Thursday.

9. What does the Arabic sentence أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I go to school on Monday.
   B. I play on Saturday.
   C. There are seven days in a week.
   D. Today is Thursday.

10. What does the Arabic word حَلْوَى (halwaa) mean? (1 mark)
   A. my turn
   B. no
   C. sweets
   D. festival

11. What does the Arabic sentence كُلَّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتُمْ بِخَيْرٍ mean? (1 mark)
   A. Blessed festival (Happy Eid).
   B. Happy birthday.
   C. May you be well every year.
   D. Do you have a party? (to a boy)

12. What does the Arabic word خُضَارٌ (khudaar) mean? (1 mark)
   A. bananas
   B. fish
   C. vegetables
   D. bread

13. What does the Arabic word بَيْضٌ (bayd) mean? (1 mark)
   A. chicken
   B. eggs
   C. meat
   D. carrots

14. Which Arabic word means "write"? (1 mark)
   A. اِلْمَسْ أَنْفَكَ
   B. افْتَحِ الْبَابَ
   C. اُكْتُبْ
   D. أَغْمِضْ عَيْنَيْكَ

15. What does the Arabic word ظَهْرٌ (dhahr) mean? (1 mark)
   A. back
   B. ear
   C. nose
   D. leg

16. What does the Arabic sentence أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي mean? (1 mark)
   A. I hear with my ear.
   B. I see with my eye.
   C. I smell with my nose.
   D. I speak with my mouth.

17. What does the Arabic word شَجَرَةٌ (shajara) mean? (1 mark)
   A. tree
   B. cloudy
   C. hot
   D. wind

18. In a short speech, what does the sentence anaa fii S-Saffi r-raabiʿ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I am in Grade 4
   B. I am at the door
   C. I am in the kitchen
   D. I am a teacher

19. How do you read the syllable قَا? (1 mark)
   A. nu
   B. da
   C. qaa
   D. ba

20. How do you read the syllable سَ? (1 mark)
   A. na
   B. sa
   C. mi
   D. li

21. How do you read the syllable ثَا? (1 mark)
   A. sa
   B. qaa
   C. lu
   D. thaa

22. What does the Arabic sentence أَخِي صَغِيرٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. My brother is small.
   B. My grandfather is old (big in age).
   C. My sister is beautiful.
   D. Hello, Ahmad.

23. The sentence ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub says where a cup is. Where is it? (1 mark)
   A. Under the bed
   B. At the door
   C. On the table
   D. In the bag

24. What does the Arabic sentence الْأَصْدِقَاءُ فِي الْحَفْلَةِ mean? (1 mark)
   A. On the table there is a cake.
   B. Above the table there is a balloon.
   C. The friends are at the party.
   D. This is a party.

25. What does maadhaa mean? (1 mark)
   A. what
   B. who
   C. why
   D. where

26. How is the Arabic word سُكَّرٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. sukkar
   B. jazar
   C. burtuqaal
   D. lahm

27. Which Arabic word means "hand"? (1 mark)
   A. لِسَانٌ
   B. رَأْسٌ
   C. يَدٌ
   D. وَجْهٌ

28. What does the ending -aani show in yadaani? (1 mark)
   A. my
   B. many
   C. the
   D. exactly two

29. Which Arabic sentence means "And the rain is from the sky." (1 mark)
   A. رَأْسِي كَبِيرٌ
   B. الشَّمْسُ فِي السَّمَاءِ
   C. وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ
   D. مَا أَجْمَلَ الْبِيئَةَ

30. Which Arabic word means "in"? (1 mark)
   A. فِي
   B. عِنْدَ
   C. بِجَانِبِ
   D. خَلْفَ

31. Which sound does the Arabic letter ل make? (1 mark)
   A. m as in mat
   B. kh, a throat sound like the ch in loch
   C. l as in lamp
   D. b as in bag

32. What is the name of the Arabic letter ث? (1 mark)
   A. haa
   B. DHaa
   C. Saad
   D. thaa

33. Which sound does the Arabic letter س make? (1 mark)
   A. s as in sun
   B. kh, a throat sound like the ch in loch
   C. t as in tap
   D. j as in jug

34. What does the Arabic word كَبِيرٌ (kabiir) mean? (1 mark)
   A. maize
   B. big
   C. Wednesday
   D. cup

35. What does the Arabic sentence الطَّاوِلَةُ صَغِيرَةٌ mean? (1 mark)
   A. The window is clean.
   B. The door is big.
   C. The table is small.
   D. The chair is new.

36. What does the Arabic word مِفْتَاحٌ (miftaah) mean? (1 mark)
   A. cup
   B. lamp
   C. key
   D. door

37. What does the Arabic sentence أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ الطَّعَامَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I have a gift.
   B. I like the party.
   C. We dance.
   D. My mother cooks the food.

38. What does the Arabic word نَعَمْ (naʿam) mean? (1 mark)
   A. balloon
   B. congratulations
   C. my turn
   D. yes

39. What does the Arabic word ذُرَةٌ (dhura) mean? (1 mark)
   A. maize
   B. fruit
   C. fish
   D. chicken

40. Which Arabic sentence means "This is rain." (1 mark)
   A. الرِّيحُ قَوِيَّةٌ
   B. الشَّمْسُ حَارَّةٌ
   C. هَذَا مَطَرٌ
   D. هَذِهِ شَمْسٌ

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write four lines of a short conversation in which two friends greet each other and ask names. Use English letters for the Arabic. (4 marks) (4 marks)

42. Explain how a spelling bee is played. (3 marks) (3 marks)

43. Translate into English: aqraʾu kitaaban yawma l-ahad (2 marks)

44. Give the steps for reading a new Arabic word. (3 marks) (3 marks)

45. Write the Arabic sounds for 'two hands' and 'two legs' and give the meaning of each ending. (3 marks) (3 marks)

46. Write in Arabic sounds and translate: 'Today is Thursday.' (2 marks) (2 marks)

47. Describe how to make a vocabulary bank of words about the home. (3 marks) (3 marks)

48. Describe the steps for learning to write a new letter. (4 marks) (4 marks)

49. Translate into English: ash-shamsu fii s-samaa'i wal-ghaymu fii s-samaa'i. (2 marks) (2 marks)

50. Spell the word الخميس by naming its letters in order. (3 marks) (3 marks)

51. Translate into English: al-asdiqaa'u fii l-hafla. (2 marks) (2 marks)

52. Translate into English: ʿindii akh wa ukht (2 marks)

53. Translate into English: fii baytii matbakh (2 marks)

54. Translate into English: anaa araa biʿaynii and atakallamu bi-famii. (2 marks) (2 marks)

55. Translate into English: haadhaa baytii (2 marks)

56. Translate into English: azuuru jaddatii yawma l-jumuʿa (2 marks)

57. Write two Arabic sentences in sounds about a celebration and translate them. (4 marks) (4 marks)

58. Name three verbal cues and say how each one helps the listener. (3 marks) (3 marks)

59. Translate into English: usaaʿidu ummii yawma s-sabt (2 marks)

60. Write three instructions about the body in Arabic sounds with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

61. Translate into English: al-jawwu mumtir (2 marks)

62. Translate into English: nuhaafidhu ʿalaa l-bii'a (2 marks)

63. Give three examples of non-verbal cues you could use when reciting a poem about weather. (3 marks) (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #11 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — How are you? (to a boy)
   كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ (kayfa haaluka?) means How are you? (to a boy).

2. C — masaa'u l-khayr
   masaa'u l-khayr means 'good evening'. sabaahu l-khayr is for the morning.

3. B — anaa
   أَنَا is read anaa and means I.

4. A — هَذَا أَبِي
   هَذَا أَبِي (haadhaa abii) means: This is my father.

5. A — My brother plays.
   أَخِي يَلْعَبُ (akhii yalʿabu) means: My brother plays.

6. D — Who is this? (a boy or man)
   مَنْ هَذَا؟ (man haadhaa?) means: Who is this? (a boy or man)

7. D — matbakh
   مَطْبَخٌ is read matbakh and means kitchen.

8. A — I play on Saturday.
   أَلْعَبُ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ (alʿabu yawma s-sabt) means: I play on Saturday.

9. A — I go to school on Monday.
   أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الِاثْنَيْنِ (adhhabu ilaa l-madrasa yawma l-ithnayn) means: I go to school on Monday.

10. C — sweets
   حَلْوَى (halwaa) means sweets.

11. C — May you be well every year.
   كُلَّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتُمْ بِخَيْرٍ (kulla ʿaamin wa-antum bi-khayr) means: May you be well every year.

12. C — vegetables
   خُضَارٌ (khudaar) means vegetables.

13. B — eggs
   بَيْضٌ (bayd) means eggs.

14. C — اُكْتُبْ
   اُكْتُبْ (uktub) means write.

15. A — back
   ظَهْرٌ (dhahr) means back.

16. C — I smell with my nose.
   أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي (ashummu bi-anfii) means: I smell with my nose.

17. A — tree
   شَجَرَةٌ (shajara) means tree.

18. A — I am in Grade 4
   Saff means class and raabiʿ means fourth.

19. C — qaa
   قَا is read qaa.

20. B — sa
   سَ is read sa.

21. D — thaa
   ثَا is read thaa.

22. A — My brother is small.
   أَخِي صَغِيرٌ (akhii Sagiir) means: My brother is small.

23. C — On the table
   ʿalaa t-taawilati kuub means 'on the table there is a cup'.

24. C — The friends are at the party.
   الْأَصْدِقَاءُ فِي الْحَفْلَةِ (al-asdiqaa'u fii l-hafla) means: The friends are at the party.

25. A — what
   maadhaa means what.

26. A — sukkar
   سُكَّرٌ is read sukkar and means sugar.

27. C — يَدٌ
   يَدٌ (yad) means hand.

28. D — exactly two
   The dual ending -aani means two, so yadaani is two hands.

29. C — وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ
   وَالْمَطَرُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ (wal-maTaru mina s-samaa'i) means: And the rain is from the sky.

30. A — فِي
   فِي (fii) means in.

31. C — l as in lamp
   The letter ل makes the sound l as in lamp.

32. D — thaa
   The letter ث is called thaa.

33. A — s as in sun
   The letter س makes the sound s as in sun.

34. B — big
   كَبِيرٌ (kabiir) means big.

35. C — The table is small.
   الطَّاوِلَةُ صَغِيرَةٌ (at-taawilatu Sagiira) means: The table is small.

36. C — key
   مِفْتَاحٌ (miftaah) means key.

37. D — My mother cooks the food.
   أُمِّي تَطْبُخُ الطَّعَامَ (ummii tatbukhu T-taʿaam) means: My mother cooks the food.

38. D — yes
   نَعَمْ (naʿam) means yes.

39. A — maize
   ذُرَةٌ (dhura) means maize.

40. C — هَذَا مَطَرٌ
   هَذَا مَطَرٌ (haadhaa matar) means: This is rain.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: A: as-salaamu ʿalaykum. B: wa ʿalaykumu s-salaam. A: maa ismuka? B: ismii Ahmad.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct line: greeting, reply, question, answer.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Teams take turns; a learner says the Arabic word and spells it by naming the letters; correct spelling earns a point.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for teams, 1 mark for spelling by letter names and 1 mark for scoring.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: I read a book on Sunday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at each letter and its mark; read each syllable; blend the syllables and check that the word makes sense.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: yadaani (two hands) and rijlaani (two legs). The ending -aani means two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word and 1 mark for the ending.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: al-yawmu yawmu l-khamiis. Today is Thursday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the Arabic sounds and 1 mark for the translation.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Write each Arabic word on a card with a picture; write the sound and meaning on the back; keep the cards in a box or on a chart and use them to practise.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid step.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Trace the model; copy it several times from right to left; write it from memory and compare; add and check the dots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun is in the sky and the clouds are in the sky.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each half.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: alif, laam, khaa, miim, yaa, siin.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for all six letters in order; 2 marks for four or five; 1 mark for two or three.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: The friends are at the party.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 'the friends' and 1 mark for 'at the party'.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: I have a brother and a sister.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

53. (2 marks)
   Answer: In my house there is a kitchen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: I see with my eye. I speak with my mouth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each translation.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: This is my house.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: I visit my grandmother on Friday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example haadhihi hafla. This is a party. ʿindii hadiyya. I have a gift.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence and 1 mark for each translation.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Intonation shows questions and statements; speed shows importance or excitement; tonal variation shows feeling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cue with its use.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: I help my mother on Saturday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: irfaʿ yadaka (raise your hand), ilmis anfaka (touch your nose), aghmiD ʿaynayka (close your eyes).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct instruction with meaning.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: The weather is rainy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

62. (2 marks)
   Answer: We look after the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

63. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lifting arms for the sun; wiggling fingers downwards for rain; smiling at the last line.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each cue that matches a word.
